walkthroughs.body_html:
Exclusivism: 'I am the way, the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me' (John 14:6).

Inclusivism: Vatican II 'Nostra Aetate' (1965) said the Church rejects nothing true and holy in other religions.

Pluralism: John Hick argued all religions are valid responses to the same divine reality.

Many religious believers see no conflict between faith and science. Catholic teaching accepts evolution (Pope John Paul II, 1996, called it 'more than a hypothesis').

Some Christians ('young-Earth creationists') read Genesis literally. Most Muslims accept scientific accounts of the universe while affirming Allah is the creator.

Christianity: Church of England has ordained women priests since 1994 and women bishops since 2014. The Catholic Church does not ordain women.

Islam: women may lead other women in prayer; mixed-congregation imams are debated. The Qur'an grants women rights to inheritance, property and education.

mcqs.q: What is substance dualism about mind and body?
options: Substance dualism means men and women are different.
The view (associated with Descartes) that mind and body are two distinct kinds of substance — a non-physical mind interacting with a physical body.
Substance dualism is the belief that humans have two personalities.
The covenant means Jews must not interact with non-Jews.

mcqs.q: What does the Abrahamic covenant in Judaism involve?
options: Being 'chosen' means Jews believe they are superior to other peoples.
The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.
God's promise to Abraham of land, descendants and blessing, in return for faithfulness — the foundational covenant marking Jews as a covenant people with responsibilities, not privileges.
The covenant means Jews must not interact with non-Jews.
